Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached are two items we discussed: the pricing matrix (aperture_pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a draft SOW that reflects a 12-month reserved commit for 120 A100-equivalent GPU months. A few points for clarity so we can get legal/procurement moving: 

- Proposed commit term: 12 months with monthly consumption reconciliation.
- Pricing umbrella: we propose a cap on per-GPU effective rate that steps with a pre-agreed market index (GPU-Index v1). Any market-driven uplift beyond the cap falls to Redwood until a threshold (see matrix).
- Fallback lanes: if market surge >25% for more than 2 consecutive months, we switch to pre-agreed fallback SKUs (lower perf) or enable phased reduction with prorated credits.
- Discount band: list shows proposed volume discounts up to 18% at commit tiers; discounts above 18% require Sales Director sign-off + Finance approval.

Can you confirm Aperture can consent to a 12-month term and the proposed escalation runway (i.e., the fallback lane mechanics)? If procurement wants a different cadence (quarterly reconciliation) we can model that too.

Samir —

Great questions — short answers below and attached an annotated pricing matrix with scenario rows (see aperture_pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx, rows 44-59 for scenarios). Quick notes: 

- GPU-Index source: we propose "GPUIndexX" (public monthly published index used by market benchmarks). We'll include the exact reference and link in the SOW so it's auditable.
- Cap mechanics: the cap is a moving threshold tied to GPUIndexX + fixed delta; when the index spikes, Redwood absorbs up to 15% of the uplift. Beyond that, the uplift is shared per the table (example scenarios attached).
- Latency SLAs under fallback: we will guarantee p50 and p90 latency bands for the fallback SKU table for inference workloads defined in Appendix B of the SOW. Credits apply automatically on monthly reconciliation as a line item credit.
- Approvers for discounts: Sales Director (Ben Carter) can approve up to 18% on standard SOWs; anything >18% requires Finance (Marcus Lin) and approval from Head of Sales Ops.

If procurement wants an explicit example: Scenario A (market +30% for two months) => Redwood applies fallback SKU for months 2-3, credits applied on month 3 reconciliation equal to 8% of billed usage for those months. Scenario B (single-month +40% spike) => Redwood absorbs first 15%, remaining applies per split in sheet.

Marcus — Monica, please confirm Finance is comfortable with the proposed approver ladder and that we have latitude for the 15% absorb clause without pre-approval.

Thanks,
Jordan
